seen.extent: Four underlined lines at the top of f. 231r, each of about 7-10 word-like groups (roughly 30-35 groups and on the order of 120-160 signs in all; estimated from the crops, not counted sign by sign), written right to left above the large-script lines 5-9
seen.cipher: A cipher text in an altered Syriac script: word groups joined and spaced as in cursive Serto, in which forms of Syriac letters (vertical alaph or lamadh strokes, mim, waw and he loops) stand together with signs shaped like Eastern Arabic numerals (a 4-shape, a 9-shape, a 2/6-shape) and signs that belong to no script, some carrying red dots in the place of Syriac diacritic points. Sample, line 1 from the right, first group as read here: a dalath/rish-like hook, a 4-shaped sign with a red dot under it, a semkath-like sign; line 4 from the right begins with a mim-like sign, a 4-shaped sign and a vertical stroke. The end of line 4 at the left has forms like Syriac lamadh-alaph ligatures. Sachau's catalogue describes the same lines as 'vier Zeilen in einer Chiffreschrift, bestehend aus Ziffern, Buchstaben und willkürlich erfundenen Zeichen'. No decipherment, gloss or key is written on f. 231r, above or between the lines, and none on f. 230v (end of the Karshuni Prayer of Solomon) or f. 231v (Syriac/Karshuni text). The plaintext language (Syriac or Karshuni Arabic) cannot be judged without reading it.
